Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

ask verb

also ask a question, ask further questions, he asked me whether, I want to ask you this, ask someone for something, why do you ask me that?, that’s not what I’m asking, ask someone something, ask for something, ask about, interrogate, question (someone)

classical

Traupman 28: pauca quaerere, to ask a few questions

quaerō, quaerere, quaesīvī, quaesītum

verb, third conjugation

seek or ask

Other words

  • rogō, rogāre, rogāvī, rogātum — ask (a question, or for something)

    verb, first conjugation; aliquem aliquid rogāre, the person and the thing both in the accusative · also used · classical · Plaut. Most. 5.1.70: aliud tē rogō (Lewis & Short); Traupman 93; Traupman 28: aliquem aliquid rogāre, to ask someone something; ab aliquō aliquid rogāre, to ask someone for something; dē aliquō rogāre, to ask about

    Classically the thing asked stands in the accusative beside the person only when it is a neuter pronoun or adjective (hoc tē rogō); otherwise rogāre aliquem dē aliquā rē (Lewis & Short). Quaerere ā (ex, dē) aliquō is to ask someone, enquire of him.

  • interrogō, interrogāre, interrogāvī, interrogātum — ask (a person) a question, question

    verb, first conjugation, with the person in the accusative · also used · classical · Plaut. (Lewis & Short): hoc quod tē interrogō, respondē; Traupman 28: docentem (discentem) interrogāre, to ask the teacher (student) a question; Traupman 334

Examples

  • aliud tē rogō

    that’s not what I’m asking youPlaut. Most. 5.1.70 (Lewis & Short)

  • quaesīvit ā medicīs quemadmodum sē habēret

    he asked the doctors how he wasNep. Dion 2.4 (Lewis & Short)

  • dēsinant quīdam quaerere ultrā aut opīnārī

    let certain people stop asking further questions or guessingSuet. Caes. 66 (Lewis & Short)

  • Hoc tē rogāre volō.

    I want to ask you this.Traupman 93

  • Quid mē istud rogās?

    Why do you ask me that?Traupman 93

See also look for, what do you want?.
